summary: The customer wants to know whether an in situ spectroscopy pilot can measure glucose and lactate in an aqueous cell culture process fast enough to replace the delay-prone sampling, checked against their existing laboratory measurements.

facts_stated.text: They run a cell culture process in an aqueous medium.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: We run a cell culture process in an aqueous medium.

facts_stated.text: Glucose and lactate are currently measured from samples.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: Glucose and lactate are measured from samples

facts_stated.text: The delay in those measurements makes it difficult to see changes promptly.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: the delay makes it difficult to see changes promptly

facts_stated.text: They are exploring an in situ spectroscopy pilot.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: We are exploring an in situ spectroscopy pilot

facts_stated.text: The pilot would be checked against the existing laboratory measurements.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: checked against those existing laboratory measurements

facts_stated.text: The medium and the cell population change during the run.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: The medium and cell population change during the run

facts_stated.text: No probe and no calibration strategy have been selected yet.

Medium composition and possible interferents or fluorescent species
Whether any fluorescent indicator or reagent would be acceptable
Pressure and any sterilisation/CIP/SIP conditions at the measurement point
Installation point and interface (bioreactor type, port, single-use vs stainless)
Distance between probe and any remote analyser
Details of the existing laboratory reference method and its uncertainty
Calibration strategy and how it would be maintained over a changing medium and cell population
